Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then stop. Do not write files, run commands or edit anything.

Attached reference images, in order:
Image 1: Geometry guide and edit target: exact silhouette, placement and scale authority; reskin it, never move or reshape it
Image 2: Material and style reference only (the existing swarm runner's matching part); match its chitin, colours and rendering, never its shape

Use case: sketch-to-render. Asset: the torso/shoulder layer of the swarm BRUTE, a heavy armoured alien strain that breaks into buildings, for a top-down tactical game. Image 1 is the authoritative geometry guide and edit target. Reskin this exact shape into a finished painted sprite, preserving its outline and placement exactly. It is a massive headless upper body seen from above: a broad domed dorsal shell of thick overlapping chitin plates (each plate a heavy scale with a worn bone-grey rim, the arcs in the guide are the plate seams), flanked by two huge armoured pauldron humps, with a dark recessed socket at the front where the separate head layer sits. It must read as far heavier and more plated than the ordinary runner: thick, scarred, battering-ram armour, a few chipped and cracked plate edges. No head, no arms, no claws, no legs, no tail, no weapons. Straight overhead orthographic zenith camera looking down on the top of the part, forward (the creature's front) is up, no perspective, no cast shadow, no ground, no floor, no border, no text, no labels, no watermark. Genuine transparent background outside the silhouette, including any negative space. Crisp hand-painted 2D strategy-game sprite matching the existing swarm creature in the material reference: dark charcoal-purple segmented chitin, organic gunmetal-green ridges and under-plates, restrained bone-grey claw and plate edges, tiny warm amber sensory nodes. It will be shown only about 40 to 90 pixels wide in play, so keep bold readable plate shapes, clear dark separations and strong value contrast rather than fine noise. Change only material, detail and subtle ambient shading; never the silhouette, placement, scale or the transparent space. The pale yellow dots in the guide mark where small glowing nodes go; they are not shapes to copy literally.
